title: A multi-target confirmation programme for a 300-390 keV inelastic splitting: xenon, iodine and tungsten as a delta-meter
question: How precisely does the W/Xe (and I/Xe) count ratio measure delta with the coupling profiled, for xenon 10-50 t yr and CaWO4 10-1000 kg yr; which windows and backgrounds does each target face; what exposures give 3 sigma between delta=300 and 380 keV and between inelastic DM and the L10 dipole; can tungsten or iodine see the endpoint E+(delta)?
headline_result: Xenon 20 t yr (5-1000 keV) plus CaWO4 100 kg yr measures delta from the W/Xe count ratio (16/82/221/693 at 300/350/366/380 keV) to sigma_delta = 99/10/3.5/0.8 keV statistically, limited by a ~15 keV halo/form-factor calibration floor (v_esc +-16 km/s -> +-13 keV, W form factor x2 -> +-12 keV) and a 20-50 keV mass degeneracy; 3 sigma inelastic-vs-L10 needs 215/17/2.1/0.09 kg yr; the tungsten endpoint (1131 keV) is unobservable (0.39% of rate above 500 keV, E99 = 410-458 keV set by a Helm node), the W shape gives 40 keV/sqrt(N) and a 700 keV ROI suffices
key_numbers: W/Xe 15.9/81.7/221/693, I/Xe 0.59/0.30/0.14/0.023, L10 W/Xe 0.05-0.07 flat, Ge 0; sigma_delta (Xe 20; CaWO4 0.01/0.1/1 t yr) 306/99/38 (300), 29/10/5.5 (350), 8.7/3.5/2.4 (366), 1.5/0.8/0.7 keV (380); biases v_esc +-16 -> +-13, FF x2 -> +-12, m=4 TeV -21, 400 GeV +38 keV; 3 sigma CaWO4: 300 vs 380 38 kg yr, 300 vs 350 1.3 t yr, inel vs L10 215/17/2.1/0.09 kg yr; E+(186W,June,366)=1131 keV, dE+/dv=4.9 keV per km/s, E+=618/1547 keV at 0.4/4 TeV; frac>500 keV 0.39%; shape 40 keV/sqrt(N) (toys 7.8 vs Fisher 7.3 keV at N=30); CaWO4 10 kg yr counts 0.04/0.41/2.9/56; 180W alpha 2.65/kg/day; radiogenic-n W recoils <=220 keV; muon-n ~20 W scatters/t yr before veto
model_or_mechanism: O1 isoscalar inelastic DM (1 TeV; 0.4/4 TeV for mass degeneracy) and L10 dipole-dipole on Xe, I, W, Ge; WimPyDD rates factorised into per-isotope kernels x Earth-frame eta(v_min); profiled-coupling multinomial Fisher information and Asimov likelihood ratios; spectral-shape Fisher, KL-projection biases, toy MLEs, order statistics; CaWO4 background arithmetic
